# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_012_page_001.jpg

---

**12:1** For your incorruptible Spirit is in all things.

**12:2** Therefore those who err you rebuke a little at a time, and in the things in which they sin you remind [them] and warn [them], that departing from evil they may believe in you, O Lord.

**12:3** For even the ancient dwellers of your holy land you hated

**12:4** for doing [works] most hateful — works of sorcery and unholy rites,

**12:5** ruthless slaughters of children, and sacrificial feasts of human flesh and blood, from the midst of an initiation,

**12:6** and parents who are slayers of helpless souls — you willed to destroy by the hands of our fathers,

**12:7** that the land most precious to you might receive a worthy colony of God's children.

**12:8** But even these, as men, you spared, and you sent hornets as forerunners of your army, so-that they might destroy them little by little.

**12:9** Not that you were unable to hand over the ungodly to the righteous in battle, or to destroy [them] at once with terrible beasts or a harsh word,

**12:10** but judging them gradually you gave [them] time for repentance, not being-ignorant that their origin was evil and their wickedness inborn, and that their way-of-thinking would not change for an age;

**12:11** for they were a cursed seed from the beginning — neither was it out-of fear of anyone that you were-letting their sins-go-unpunished.

**12:12** For who will say, "What have you done?" or who will resist your judgment? And who will bring charges against you for the destruction of nations which you made? Or who will come against you as an advocate for unrighteous men?

**12:13** For neither is there any god beside you who cares for all, to whom you might show that you have not judged unjustly,

**12:14** nor can [any] king or ruler confront you in defense of those you have punished.

**12:15** Being righteous yourself, you govern all things righteously, considering it alien to your power to condemn one who does-not deserve to-be-punished.

**12:16** For your strength is the beginning of righteousness, and your sovereignty over all things makes you forbearing toward all.

**12:17** For you show strength when the perfection of your power is not believed, and you reprove presumptuousness in those who know [it].

**12:18** But you, mastering strength, judge with forbearance and govern us with great reserve; for the power is present to you whenever you will it.

**12:19** But you taught your people through such deeds that the righteous man must be a friend to men, and you gave good hope to your sons that you give repentance for sins.

**12:20** For if with such great care and forbearance you punished the enemies of your children and who deserved-to-die, giving [them] times and opportunity by which they might be-released from evil,

**12:21** with how great precision did you judge your sons, to whose fathers you gave oaths and covenants of good promises!

**12:22** Therefore while disciplining us you scourge our enemies a thousand-fold, so-that when judging we might think on your goodness, and when judged we might await mercy.

**12:23** Hence also those who lived in folly and unrighteousness you tormented through their own abominations.

**12:24** For they wandered far astray in the paths of error, taking as gods those things that are despised even among animals, being deceived like thoughtless children.

**12:25** Therefore as to unreasoning children you sent a judgment in mockery.

**12:26** But those who were-not corrected by mockery-judgments will experience the worthy judgment of God.

**12:27** For over what things they were-indignant when suffering — through these things, which they thought gods, being punished in them, they saw and recognized the one who truly is God, whom they had previously refused to know — therefore also the complete condemnation came upon them.
